chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Ali (peace be upon him) did not increase upon cutting the hand and the leg, and he said: 'I am shy of my Lord that I should leave him without having for him what he uses for cleansing after relieving himself or purifying himself with.'
He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him, if he were to steal after the cutting of the hand and the leg?' So he said: 'I would keep him in prison forever, and spare the people from his evil.'

key_terms.قَطْعُ الْيَدِ وَالرِّجْلِ: Cutting of the hand and the foot (hadd punishment for theft)
key_terms.يَسْتَنْجِي: Cleansing oneself after relieving oneself with water or stones

ai.seo_question: What is the limit of the punishment for theft according to Imam Ali (peace be upon him) and what happens if he steals again?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) precise application of the hadd punishment for theft, emphasizing that the cutting of the hand and foot is the complete statutory penalty, ensuring the thief retains sufficient limb for ritual purification (istinja). It further establishes the principle of indefinite imprisonment for recidivists to protect the community, reflecting the Shia juristic view that the hadd is fixed and not subject to arbitrary augmentation by the judge. This practice underscores the balance between strict adherence to divine law and practical social welfare in early Islamic governance.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from someone else, from Aban Bin Usman, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> did not increased upon cutting of the hand and the leg, and he<sup>asws</sup> was saying, I<sup>asws</sup> am embarassed from my<sup>asws</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup> that I<sup>asws</sup> should leave him not having for him what he can wash himself with (from toilet), or clean himself with’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘If he were to steal after cutting of the hand and the leg?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> would leave him in the prison forever, and make the people to be free from his evil’.
